title: IMF Raises India Growth Forecast to 7% as Global Outlook Fragments
excerpt: Citing resilient domestic demand and services, the IMF lifted India's FY27 forecast by 60 basis points — even as it projects just 3.1% global growth in 2026 and warns that world resilience is wearing thin.
body:
• The IMF raised India's FY27 growth forecast by 60 basis points to 7%, citing resilient domestic demand and robust services activity despite higher oil prices.
  • India remains among the fastest-growing major economies: the IMF projects global growth of just 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, and advanced economies at 1.8% in 2027.
  • The upgrade follows a run of revisions — the RBI now expects 7.1% for FY27, the World Bank raised its forecast to 7.1%, and the OECD lifted its call to 7.1%.
  • What it means for your money: the IMF expects India's inflation to average 5% in FY27, up from 2% in FY26 — a path that limits how fast the RBI can cut rates, even as growth holds up.

The International Monetary Fund has raised India's growth forecast for the fiscal year 2026-27 to 7%, an upgrade of 60 basis points, in its latest World Economic Outlook released during the Fund's annual meetings in Bangkok. "India's growth remained robust, underpinned by domestic demand and services, despite higher oil prices," the IMF said, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The Fund also projects 7% growth for the following year.

A chorus of upgrades

The IMF is not alone. Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India raised its real GDP growth projection for FY27 to 7.1% from 6.7%. The World Bank raised its forecast for the current fiscal year by 50 basis points to 7.1%, while cautioning that growth may slow in the second half. The OECD lifted its FY27 call by 80 basis points to 7.1%, and the Asian Development Bank, S&P and Fitch have all moved their estimates to around 7%, helped by a strong June quarter — India's GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27.

The global contrast

The upgrade stands out against a subdued world backdrop. The IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, with China's expansion easing to 4.5% and then 4%. Medium-term global growth, at an average of 3.2% a year for 2028-31, sits below the pre-pandemic average of 3.7% — and the IMF said the medium-term downgrades are concentrated in economies hit by the Middle East conflict and energy-importing emerging markets, with India an exception. The Fund's separate stability report, covered in our report on the IMF's AI crash warning, shows the other side of the same outlook.

The risks: oil and inflation

The brighter forecast rests on assumptions that could break. The IMF's projections assume average crude oil prices of $95.74 a barrel in 2026, about 41% higher than 2025, easing to $87.39 in 2027. For a major oil importer, sustained prices at those levels raise the import bill, widen the current account deficit — which the Fund expects to reach 1.5% of GDP in FY27 — and feed inflation. The IMF projects India's consumer inflation at 5% in FY27 before moderating to 4.4% in FY28.

What it means for diaspora investors

For NRIs with money in Indian equities, deposits and property, the IMF's message is two-sided. A 7% growth path supports corporate earnings and the long-term case for Indian assets. But 5% inflation alongside it argues against expecting rapid rate cuts: NRE and NRO deposit rates are unlikely to fall quickly, and borrowers in India face a longer stretch of elevated rates. The variable to watch is oil — the single assumption on which both the growth upgrade and the inflation forecast depend.

What's next

The next tests come quickly: monthly inflation prints through the festive quarter, the RBI's December policy review, and whether oil holds near the IMF's assumed path. If crude breaks higher, expect the growth upgrades to be revisited as fast as they arrived.
